transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The most likely causes are moisture tracking under the glass (if there was a spill) or a fault in the internal power module/coil. Please stop using the hob immediately. Do not try to reset the breaker repeatedly to keep cooking; that is unsafe. To help narrow this down: has there been any recent spillage on or around the hob that might have seeped underneath? If so, has it had several days to dry out completely?
Yes, there have been a couple of boil-overs. Also, after one of the trips I noticed a faint electrical smell, just the once. I'm not sure how long it had to dry out.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Given the boil-overs and that electrical smell, it is highly likely that liquid seeped underneath the glass and caused an earth leak, or that a component inside has been damaged by heat. Because this involves mains electricity and a potential fire risk, you must not use the hob again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. They will need to isolate the unit, dry out any moisture, and test the internal power modules for faults. Please contact an appliance repair service or your local electrician to arrange a visit.
